provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Revision of singing
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to sing familiar songs in tune.
The pupils should be able to perform warm up exercises.
Introduction:
We have learned many songs before. Today we will sing them again.
Content:
Warm up songs help our voices. We do them before singing.
We sing in tune when we follow the high and low sounds.
Class activity:
The whole class will sing Old MacDonald together.
Evaluation questions:
What do we do before singing?
Can you name one warm up song?
Show me how to sing high notes.
Summary:
Today we practiced singing in tune and did warm up songs.

topics.title: Drawing: things in the home
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to draw a simple chair.
The pupils should be able to draw a cup.
Introduction:
We see chairs and cups in our homes every day.
Today we will learn to draw them.
Content:
A chair has four legs and a flat seat to sit on.
A cup has a handle and holds water or tea.
Class activity:
Each pupil will draw a chair and a cup on paper.
Evaluation questions:
What part of the chair do we sit on?
How many legs does a chair have?
What do we use a cup for?
Summary:
We learned to draw simple things from our homes.

topics.title: Designing patterns
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to make a repeat pattern.
The pupils should be able to create a border design.
Introduction:
Patterns are designs that repeat again and again.
We see patterns on our clothes and in our homes.
Content:
A repeat pattern uses the same shape over and over.
A border design goes around the edge of paper.
Class activity:
Pupils will make patterns with coloured pencils on paper.
Evaluation questions:
What is a pattern?
Where can we see patterns?
How do we make a border design?
Summary:
We learned to make patterns and border designs.

topics.title: Rhythm: clapping patterns
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to echo clap a rhythm.
The pupils should be able to keep a steady beat.
Introduction:
We make music with our bodies too.
Today we will learn to clap rhythms.
Content:
Echo clapping means copying a rhythm after hearing it.
Keeping the beat means clapping at the same speed.
Class activity:
The teacher claps a pattern and pupils copy it.
Evaluation questions:
What is echo clapping?
How do we keep a steady beat?
Show me a clapping pattern.
Summary:
We practiced clapping rhythms and keeping the beat.

topics.title: Traditional songs of my area
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to sing a local song.
The pupils should be able to sing in a group.
Introduction:
Every part of Nigeria has special songs.
Today we will learn songs from our area.
Content:
Traditional songs tell stories about our people.
Singing in groups means many voices together.
Class activity:
Pupils will sing a traditional song in small groups.
Evaluation questions:
What are traditional songs?
Why do we sing in groups?
Name one traditional song you know.
Summary:
We learned to sing traditional songs together.

topics.title: Craft: papier mache basics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to tear and soak paper.
The pupils should be able to make a simple bowl.
Introduction:
We can make things from old paper and paste.
This craft is called papier mache.
Content:
First we tear paper into small pieces.
Then we soak the paper and paste it to make shapes.
Class activity:
Pupils will make a small bowl using papier mache.
Evaluation questions:
What is papier mache?
What do we do first with the paper?
What can we make with papier mache?
Summary:
We learned to make simple things with papier mache.

topics.title: Clay work: animals
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to mould a clay animal.
The pupils should be able to display their work.
Introduction:
We can make animals using soft clay.
Clay comes from the earth and we can shape it.
Content:
We roll clay in our hands to make shapes.
We can make animals like goats and birds with clay.
Class activity:
Each pupil will mould a goat or bird from clay.
Evaluation questions:
What can we make with clay?
Show me how to roll clay.
What animal did you make?
Summary:
We made animal shapes from clay.

topics.title: Drama: classroom scenes
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to act as a teacher.
The pupils should be able to act as a pupil.
Introduction:
We can pretend to be different people.
This is called acting or drama.
Content:
In drama we pretend to be someone else.
We can act scenes from our classroom.
Class activity:
Pupils will act a simple classroom scene with teacher and pupil.
Evaluation questions:
What is drama?
How do we act like a teacher?
What happens in a classroom scene?
Summary:
We learned to act in a simple play.

topics.title: Movement to music
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to march to music.
The pupils should be able to gallop to music.
Introduction:
Our bodies can move to music.
Different music makes us move in different ways.
Content:
Marching means walking with high steps like soldiers.
Galloping means running with one foot leading.
Class activity:
Pupils will march and gallop when the teacher plays music.
Evaluation questions:
How do we march?
Show me how to gallop.
How does music make us move?
Summary:
We learned to move our bodies to music.

topics.title: Revision and assessment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to show what they learned.
The pupils should be able to display their work.
Introduction:
Today we will remember what we learned this term.
We will show our best work to the class.
Content:
We will sing songs, draw pictures and show crafts.
Each pupil will talk about their favorite thing.
Class activity:
Pupils will display their work around the classroom.
Evaluation questions:
What did you learn this term?
Which activity did you like most?
Show me your best work.
Summary:
We showed all the things we learned this term.
